entries.test: Public evaluations of systems available in October 2023 on counting, five-digit multiplication, kinship relations, chess legality, factual writing, and driving would test these asserted limitations.
entries.note: Read in context as a claim about contemporary AI capabilities and reliability. The driving clause reports an absence of demonstrated performance.
This assesses the paper's argumentative merit and treatment of critics.

entries.test: Publicly documented comparisons of the child's and contemporary LLMs' accuracy on comparable five-digit multiplication problems would settle the performance claim.
entries.note: The child's performance could be publicly demonstrated; currently private evidence does not make the claim inherently uncheckable.
The main assertion judges a presumption as overreach. The concession about achieved prerequisites is explicitly tentative.
The central claim evaluates whether these capabilities warrant the general-intelligence label. Its supporting performance assertions are separately testable.

entries.test: Published descriptions and comparative evaluations of practical AI systems in the named fields would show their use of alternative architectures and their relative tractability, reliability, and efficiency.
entries.note: The preceding sentences concern use of the transformer architecture broadly. Restricting the proposition to transformer-based LLMs narrows that scope.

entries.test: Public attention, documented applications, and comparative performance across the practical AI tasks named in the post would test their prominence, utility, and limitations as all-purpose tools in October 2023.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give the all-purpose-tools claim a concrete capability reading.

entries.test: Public evaluations and documented applications of the generation succeeding October 2023 systems would show whether abilities and applications expanded and existing weaknesses diminished.
entries.note: “No doubt” expresses a firm forecast. Successor generations have appeared by the evaluation date.
This judges the justification for applying the general-intelligence label, rather than specifying an independently testable capability threshold.
